4. Neural Network Terms

  • Neuron / Unit — one weighted sum + activation.
  • Layer — a group of neurons applied together (Linear, Conv2d, Attention).
  • Depth — number of layers; controls representational power.
  • Width — number of units per layer; controls capacity.
  • Skip connection — residual add that eases gradient flow.

5. PyTorch Vocabulary

  • nn.Module — base class for models & layers.
  • forward() — defines the computation; called via model(x).
  • state_dict() — dict of parameter tensors, used for save/load.
  • torch.no_grad() — disables autograd for inference.
  • DataLoader, Dataset, Sampler — data pipeline building blocks.
  • torch.compile — graph capture + kernel fusion for speedups.

6. Optimization Terms

  • Learning rate — step size along the negative gradient.
  • Momentum — exponential average of gradients.
  • Weight decay — pulls weights toward zero each step.
  • Warmup — LR ramps up before decaying.
  • Gradient accumulation — sum grads across micro-batches before stepping.

7. Evaluation Metrics

  • Accuracy / Top-k — classification correctness.
  • Precision / Recall / F1 — imbalanced classification quality.
  • ROC-AUC / PR-AUC — threshold-independent ranking quality.
  • Perplexity — language-model quality; lower is better.
  • BLEU / ROUGE / METEOR — text-generation overlap metrics.
  • IoU / mAP — detection and segmentation.

8. Transformer Terminology

  • Token / Vocabulary — discrete units the model sees.
  • Positional encoding — injects order (sinusoidal, RoPE, ALiBi).
  • Causal mask — prevents attending to future tokens.
  • Context length — max tokens the model can attend over.
  • KV-cache — reused K/V during decoding for O(1) growth per step.

9. Mathematical Concepts

  • Chain rule — foundation of backprop.
  • Jacobian — matrix of first-order partials.
  • Softmax — normalises a vector to a probability distribution.
  • KL divergence — asymmetric distance between distributions.
  • Entropy — expected information content.

10. Interview Vocabulary

  • Bias-variance trade-off, regularisation, dropout, early stopping.
  • Vanishing / exploding gradients, residual connections, normalisation.
  • Transformer vs RNN, attention complexity, KV-cache.
  • Fine-tuning vs LoRA, PEFT, RLHF, DPO.
  • Quantisation, distillation, pruning.

12. Revision Sheet

  • Every activation is non-linear — otherwise deep nets collapse to a single linear map.
  • Normalisation stabilises training; residuals keep gradients alive.
  • Attention = content lookup; complexity is quadratic in sequence length.
  • Optimisers differ mostly in how they scale & smooth gradients.
  • PEFT lets you fine-tune huge models on modest hardware.

FAQ

How do I memorise this?
Read in chunks by section, then test yourself using the Quick Lookup Index.
Is BatchNorm still used?
Yes for CNNs; transformers overwhelmingly use LayerNorm / RMSNorm.
LoRA vs adapters?
LoRA edits weights via low-rank deltas; adapters insert small trainable modules. LoRA is dominant today.
